sentence: A tiny muscle on every hair pulls.
claim: In the skin, sympathetic nerve impulses trigger contraction of the arrector pili muscle (APM), pulling the hair erect: piloerection, or goosebumps.
note: [SOURCE-READ] PMC7540726 introduction: 'elevated impulses from sympathetic nerves trigger the contraction of APM bundles, pulling the hair erect, a phenomenon known as piloerection or goosebumps.' A person opens the source; dermatologist sign-off required.

sentence: Cold makes nerves in your skin send a signal.
claim: Environmental stimuli such as cold raise sympathetic nerve impulses, which trigger the muscle to contract.
note: [SOURCE-READ] PMC7540726: 'Environmental stimuli, such as cold temperatures, have a pronounced effect on the tri-lineage unit: elevated impulses from sympathetic nerves trigger the contraction of APM bundles'. A person opens the source; dermatologist sign-off required.

sentence: That signal tells a tiny muscle beside each hair to tighten.

sentence: Under the skin, each tiny muscle is woven through with nerve fibres.

sentence: In people, that no longer helps keep us warm.

sentence: Yet the muscle, the nerve and the follicle are still wired together across mammals.
claim: The hair follicle, arrector pili muscle and sympathetic nerve form a tri-lineage unit that is highly conserved across mammals, including humans.
